pages: Oswin Grale, fifty-one, tall, grey at the temples, a dark brown wool coat over a white collar, climbs the worn stone stair in the corner of the toll-house, one hand on the oak step-block at the bottom tread. Middle distance: nine treads hollow down the middle, a low hearth. Background: the one room at the gate, market morning. Warm hearth glow, cold blue doorway shade.

Sella Roke, thirteen, straight dark hair to her jaw, an oatmeal serge dress and a deep green knitted shawl, sits at a deal table turning a heavy toll-book with both hands. Middle distance: a brass lamp, a candle burnt down to the holder. Background: the one room of the toll-house at the Marrow Gate, evening. Warm lamplight against a cold blue window.

Sella Roke, thirteen, straight dark hair to her jaw, an oatmeal serge dress and a deep green knitted shawl, leans over the open toll-book on the deal table, brow down, one hand flat on the page. Middle distance: a wooden yardstick, a barley bushel measure. Background: the toll-house room, late morning. Warm light from the doorway, cold blue shade behind.

Sella Roke, thirteen, straight dark hair to her jaw, an oatmeal serge dress and a deep green knitted shawl, stands in the toll-house doorway with one hand flat on the worn oak jamb, head tilted to study it. Middle distance: the open door, an oak step-block. Background: the Marrow Gate and the market road, mid-morning. Bright daylight behind, cold blue shade inside.

Doff Pike, eighty-one, a lean old mason with thin white hair and a dusty brown waistcoat, climbs the worn stone stair with a chalk line and a plumb bob in his hands. Middle distance: nine treads hollow down the middle, an oak step-block at the foot. Background: the low-ceilinged toll-house room, spring morning. Warm light from the doorway.

Doff Pike, eighty-one, lean, thin white hair, a dusty brown waistcoat over a grey shirt, stands at the top of the stone stair with a plumb bob hanging from his fingers, looking down the flight. Middle distance: his chalk line stretched across the stair, his old coat on the newel post. Background: the toll-house room below, low beams. Warm light from a small window.

Doff Pike, eighty-one, thin white hair, a dusty brown waistcoat, stands in the toll-house doorway hauling a worn brown coat over his shoulders, one hand on the frame. Middle distance: his plumb bob and chalk line on the top step, an oak step-block below. Background: the Marrow Gate road, cold spring afternoon. Doorway light on his white hair.

Sella Roke, thirteen, straight dark hair to her jaw, an oatmeal serge dress and a deep green knitted shawl, stands at the toll-gate with the toll-book under one arm and a short knife in her hand, chin lifted to a board high on the gate post. Middle distance: the bolted gate, a bushel measure. Background: the market road, overcast morning. Flat daylight, one warm lantern.

Fenn Roke, seventy, spare, wispy white hair, a brown wool coat over a collarless shirt, sits at the deal table with the toll-book open before him, one hand flat on the page, his eyes filmy at the edges. Middle distance: a brass lamp, a walking stick leaning on the table. Background: the toll-house room, late afternoon. Warm lamplight, cold blue window shade.

Tam Roke, eight, a small barefoot boy with straight dark hair and a short brown tunic, stands on two blocks of pale ash with both arms stretched up toward a shelf above his head. Middle distance: the wall shelf, a clay cup on it. Background: a low cottage room by the hearth, lamplight hour. Warm hearth glow behind him, cold blue at the window.

Nell Grale, six, a small girl in a red wool dress with fair hair in a long plait, stands on two stacked deal boxes under the toll-house window, chin level with the sill, looking up. Middle distance: one more box on the floor, a besom in the corner. Background: the one room of the toll-house, market morning. Warm window light on her red dress.

Sella Roke, thirteen, straight dark hair to her jaw, an oatmeal serge dress and a deep green knitted shawl, kneels at the toll-house wall and lifts a bar of ash a foot wide from its socket, an iron foot and a brass nail at the top. Middle distance: the socket, a yardstick. Background: the toll-house room, mid-morning. Warm doorway light, cold shade on the stone.

Sella Roke, thirteen, straight dark hair to her jaw, an oatmeal serge dress and a deep green knitted shawl, holds the ash bar level across her hip, one end under the brass nail in the wall, eyes on the bar. Middle distance: the bar itself, the toll-book open on the table. Background: the toll-house room, Friday morning. Warm doorway light, cold shade in the corners.

Sella Roke, thirteen, straight dark hair cut level to her jaw, an oatmeal serge dress and a deep green knitted shawl, stands square in the toll-house doorway with one hand flat on the jamb, waiting. Middle distance: the open oak door, a carpenter's mallet on the step, the deal table inside. Background: the Marrow Gate, late morning. Light through the doorway, long shadow on the step.

Sella Roke, thirteen, straight dark hair to her jaw, an oatmeal serge dress and a deep green knitted shawl, stands on the toll-house step with the ash bar upright in one hand and the toll-book in the other, head up, calling the day's figures. Middle distance: the brass nail, an oak step-block. Background: the gate and the market road, market morning. Sun on her shawl.

Sella Roke, thirteen, straight dark hair to her jaw, an oatmeal serge dress and a deep green knitted shawl, stands at the toll-house door with the toll-book flat in both hands at chest height, chin level, refusing. Middle distance: the ash bar against the wall, the deal table. Background: the one room of the toll-house, late morning. Warm door light, cold blue shade behind.

Oswin Grale, fifty-one, tall, grey at the temples, a dark brown wool coat over a white collar, stands with his back flat against the stone wall beside the stair, hat off, shoulders squared. Middle distance: the ash bar and brass nail, an oak step-block. Background: the toll-house room, market day. Warm light across the stone, cold blue doorway shade.

Widow Hask, sixty, stooped, a grey shawl over a brown skirt, stands at the toll-house door with a bushel measure of barley at her hip, one hand on the sill, smiling. Middle distance: the ash bar and brass nail in the wall, the threshold stone. Background: the Marrow Gate road, market morning. Warm sun on the barley, cold blue shade in the doorway.

Oswin Grale, fifty-one, tall, grey at the temples, a dark brown wool coat, stands at the foot of the worn stone stair with one hand flat on the newel post, looking up the flight. Middle distance: the oak step-block, a bundle of old books tied with cord on the bottom tread. Background: the toll-house room, late afternoon before frost. Warm low sun through the door.

Tam Roke, eight, a small barefoot boy with straight dark hair and a short brown tunic, stands on the bare floor of a low cottage room, one hand on a wall shelf he can now reach, a clay cup set on it. Middle distance: an oak step-block put away against the wall. Background: spring morning, a small window. Warm spring sun, soft green light.
